  {
    "name_han": "七真年谱",
    "logic_thesis": "This text proves that Quanzhen orthodoxy is historically verifiable rather than merely mythic: legitimacy is generated by synchronized, datable lives of Wang Chongyang and the Seven Perfected. By collapsing eight biographies into one chronological frame, it argues that collective time-discipline—not isolated miracle—constitutes the real transmission of the Dao.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: a living lineage must be reconstructed as continuous, dated events, not floating hagiography.
2) Inference: Wang Chongyang’s conversion of seven disciples is the causal hinge of later Quanzhen expansion.
3) Inference: each Perfected’s subsequent itinerary, hardship, and teaching is evidence of the same method under different temperaments.
4) Inference: chronological alignment converts personal cultivation stories into public institutional history.
5) Conclusion: Quanzhen authority rests on demonstrable succession in historical time, which is itself a spiritual proof of “completing the true.”",
    "logic_practice": "1) When reading a BaZi chart, treat the natal pattern as a “谱” (register): map decade luck as sequential stages of a life-lineage, not random fortune.
2) Extract one core discipline from each Seven Perfected style (clear mind, endurance, stillness, social service) and match it to the chart’s weak element.
3) Use historical dates as models for timing renunciation or career pivots in the current luck cycle.
4) Practice “collective verification”: check cultivation progress against measurable life events, as the nianpu does against chronology.
5) Treat teacher–disciple transfer as a timed transmission event; note stem-branch years of initiation for lineage work.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike pure miracle hagiographies, this work subordinates marvel to calendar. It differs from 金莲正宗记 by prioritizing year-by-year sequence over narrative glory, and differs from purely doctrinal Quanzhen texts by proving the path through temporal evidence rather than abstract xingming theory."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "终南山祖庭仙真内传",
    "logic_thesis": "The text argues that place is a causal agent of sanctity: Zhongnan Mountain’s ancestral court concentrates earlier Daoist virtue so later Quanzhen can inherit it as spatial transmission. Inner biography of “仙真” proves that orthodoxy is not invented at one founder but accumulated in a sacred geography that selects and ripens adepts.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: authentic Dao must have a stable “祖庭” (ancestral court) where true persons gather across generations.
2) Inference: earlier immortals of Zhongnan form a pre-Quanzhen spiritual deposit.
3) Inference: Wang Chongyang and his heirs re-activate that deposit rather than create a vacuum religion.
4) Inference: biography of place-bound immortals legitimates institutional claim to the mountain.
5) Conclusion: geographic continuity equals doctrinal continuity; the mountain “remembers” the Dao.",
    "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi, treat strong mountain/earth structures (辰戌丑未, 艮坤) as “祖庭” nodes—places where ancestral qi can be cultivated.
2) When luck shifts to earth or mountain-related branches, prioritize retreat, temple practice, or root-clearing over travel.
3) Map personal “sacred sites” (birthplace, teacher’s mountain, burial of parents) as transmission fields.
4) Use inner biography method: write your own cultivation chronology tied to places, not only moods.
5) For lineage work, verify whether a method has a stable “court” (school form) or is free-floating charisma.",
    "logic_compare": "Compared with 七真年谱, this text proves by sacred space rather than calendar alone. Unlike pure Shangqing mountain-revelation scriptures, it is Quanzhen-historiographical: it harnesses older Zhongnan lore to authorize a new school’s claim to the ancestral seat."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太微帝君二十四神回元经",
    "logic_thesis": "It proves that the body is already a full pantheon: twenty-four gods of the three regions are not external deities but structural officers of jing, qi, and spirit. “Returning to origin” is accomplished by naming, visualizing, and reinstalling these officers so that scattered vitality re-coheres into the Taiwei order.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: human form is generated by mixed qi and therefore contains named inner deities as functional centers.
2) Inference: disease, leakage, and death are failures of those officers to stay at their posts.
3) Inference: cunsi (visualization) of names and colors reassigns each god to its region.
4) Inference: prolonged reinstallation opens the “return to yuan,” dissolving fetal knots and stagnation.
5) Conclusion: immortality technique is administrative restoration of the body-state under Taiwei Emperor’s hierarchical order.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Divide practice into three octaves (upper/middle/lower eight gods) aligned with three dantian and three BaZi “talents” (spirit, officer, wealth).
2) On the birth day or monthly jing day, recite the 24 names while scanning the corresponding body zones.
3) When a chart shows scattered 印/食伤 (leaking resources), treat it as gods off-post; use stillness to “call them back.”
4) Pair each god with a color–direction correspondence for microcosmic orientation.
5) Measure progress by cohesion of attention and reduced leakage (senses, speech, desire), not visionary fireworks.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike Beidou liturgical texts that petition external star-lords, this scripture interiorizes the hierarchy into body-gods. It differs from later neidan’s abstract three treasures by retaining early Shangqing polytheistic administration as the logic of unity."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太上紫微中天七元真经",
    "logic_thesis": "The text proves that destiny is editable at the register level: the Seven Yuan of the Northern Dipper hold the ledger of life, so ritual sound, light, and talisman can rewrite entries of disaster and lifespan. Cosmic government at Purple Tenuity is not fatalism; it is a bureaucracy open to lawful petition.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: human lifespan and calamity are recorded under the Seven Dipper lords.
2) Inference: each lord governs a distinct mode of protection (birth, obstacle-removal, illness, etc.).
3) Inference: recitation, lamp-offering, and visualization create a legal channel to those registers.
4) Inference: when the name is “noted above,” form and hun-po are guarded.
5) Conclusion: salvation is ledger correction under Zhongtian Zǐwēi, not mere psychological comfort.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Map the seven Dipper stars to the seven day-masters’ typical crisis modes; choose the matching mantra for the active luck crisis.
2) On the monthly Dipper days or birth hour, perform lamp-and-incense petition focused on one lord, not all at once.
3) In BaZi terms, treat severe 七杀/羊刃 years as “register pressure”; use 七元 work as official appeal, not denial of pattern.
4) Combine oral spell with steady breath so “sound” actually enters the body register.
5) Keep a simple response log (sleep, omens, event shifts) to verify ledger change without superstition.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike 太微二十四神回元经’s inward body bureaucracy, this text works an outer stellar bureaucracy. It is leaner and more liturgical than the longer Beidou benming scriptures, focusing on seven modular spells rather than full narrative theology."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "洞真太上三九素语玉精真诀",
    "logic_thesis": "It proves that pure speech is an ontological key: “three-nine plain words” are not poetry but engineered phonemes that open the nine orifices and three palaces. Jade-essence truth is recovered when correct sound unlocks closed spirit-gates, making longevity a function of linguistic precision rather than brute force effort.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: the body has sealed spirit-gates (ling guan) that ordinary thought cannot open.
2) Inference: primordial emperors condensed “素语” as keys to those gates.
3) Inference: timed silent/voiced recitation on benming days reorders qi in nine holes and three palaces.
4) Inference: when gates open, organs freshen, complexion becomes jade-like, and true beings respond.
5) Conclusion: verbal formula is a technical instrument of physiological and celestial access.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Practice short, exact recitation rather than long discursive prayer; precision beats volume.
2) Schedule work on the natal day (本命日) when the chart’s “door” is naturally more permeable.
3) Coordinate three palaces (head–chest–abdomen) with nine breaths as a 3×9 structure.
4) If BaZi shows sealed 印星 or blocked 食伤 (expression blocked), use plain-word practice to open the speech–spirit circuit.
5) Keep secrecy and vow discipline: the text’s logic treats leakage of formula as loss of charge.",
    "logic_compare": "Compared with Lingbao “inner sounds of the heavens,” this is Shangqing body-gate technology rather than multi-heaven salvation liturgy. It differs from later mantric popularism by insisting on elite transmission, timed use, and physiological gate theory."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "上清外国放品青童内文",
    "logic_thesis": "The text proves that true power is topographic knowledge of non-ordinary realms: foreign countries, hidden lands, and thirty-six heavens are structured domains whose secret names grant mobility, exorcism, and immunity. Salvation is cartographic—knowing the right graph and sound lets the adept cross boundaries that trap the uninitiated.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: the cosmos contains graded “foreign products/realms” beyond ordinary geography.
2) Inference: each realm has inner names, graphs, and sounds that function as passports.
3) Inference: wearing, reciting, or visualizing these texts enrolls the adept in those jurisdictions.
4) Inference: enrollment subdues demons, opens mountains, and enables spirit travel.
5) Conclusion: liberation is mastery of sacred topology via the Azure Lad’s transmitted inner writing.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Treat BaZi’s four pillars as a personal “map of realms”; identify blocked directions as locked countries.
2) When luck moves into travel or 驿马 years, pair ordinary movement with name-recitation for protection.
3) Use directional talismanic focus (east text for east crises, etc.) instead of generic prayer.
4) In meditation, practice “border crossing”: leave sensory realm, enter named heaven, return with stable identity.
5) Apply exorcistic logic ethically: name what binds you (habit, ghostly fear, social hex) and revoke its jurisdiction.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike body-god cunsi texts that stay inside the flesh, this scripture expands outward into cosmic ethnography. It differs from Lingbao universal heavens by retaining Shangqing elite secrecy and “foreign country” adventure structure under the Azure Lad transmission."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "嵩山太无先生气经",
    "logic_thesis": "It proves a strict causal law of embodiment: form depends on qi; qi depends on form; therefore longevity is engineered by staged internal breathing, not by swallowing external cosmic winds. True method is progressive interiorization from coarse regulation to fetal breath, grounded in “my destiny is in me.”",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: form and qi are mutually constitutive; lose one and the other dies.
2) Inference: external qi methods are crude and can harm if interior is not ready.
3) Inference: genuine work uses the body’s own internal qi through graded arts (调、咽、行、炼、闭, etc.).
4) Inference: constancy plus emptiness of desire allows true qi to descend and stabilize.
5) Conclusion: destiny is reclaimed by disciplined neigì sequence, not fatalist heaven or random gulping of air.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Begin with environment and schedule (dry quiet room, post-midnight or empty stomach) before advanced retention.
2) Sequence practice: expel turbid → regulate → swallow saliva-qi → move → refine → entrust → close.
3) In BaZi weak-qi charts (feeble 日主, damaged 印), prioritize gentle neigì over aggressive fasting.
4) Use grip-seal (握固) only after circulation is open, matching the text’s staged caution.
5) Track sweat, warmth, calm hunger, and sleep as objective markers of qi sufficiency.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike Shangqing visionary pantheons, this is technical respiratory engineering. Compared with 中黄真经, it is more stepwise pedagogical and less focused on grain-toxin theory; compared with 五厨经, it is more somatic technique than mind-nourishment philosophy."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太上肘后玉经方",
    "logic_thesis": "The text argues that the highest method must be portable and immediately usable—“behind the elbow,” always at hand. Jade-scripture formulas compress esoteric efficacy into compact prescriptions, proving that Daoist truth is not only grand cosmology but emergency-ready operational knowledge.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: adepts face sudden crises that lengthy ritual cannot address in time.
2) Inference: authentic transmission therefore includes condensed “elbow-side” formulas.
3) Inference: compact jade methods retain full structural logic of larger systems in miniature.
4) Inference: diligent private application produces spiritual effect without institutional theater.
5) Conclusion: true mastery is the ability to deploy the Dao as a pocketed, exact remedy.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Distill your BaZi remedy into 1–3 “elbow formulas” (one breath pattern, one behavioral vow, one timing rule).
2) Keep a daily micro-protocol that can be done in under ten minutes under stress.
3) Prefer small consistent doses of practice over rare grand retreats.
4) When luck is chaotic, use the portable method first; expand only after stability returns.
5) Record which compact formula works for which pillar stress (wealth month vs officer year).",
    "logic_compare": "It differs from encyclopedic qi scriptures by valuing brevity and readiness. Unlike imperial Daodejing commentaries that scale Dao to statecraft, this is field medicine for the solitary body—operational Dao rather than metaphysical exposition."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "长生胎元神用经",
    "logic_thesis": "It proves that longevity is the correct mother–child relation of qi and spirit: qi is mother, spirit is child; the child must ride the mother’s breath without losing the embryonic pearl. Long life is not accumulation of years but continuous re-enactment of the original generative bond inside the lower yuan.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: what generates life (胎元) can also regenerate life if repaired.
2) Inference: form arises from subtle qi; spirit arises after form-qi are established.
3) Inference: disordered thought breaks the mother–child link and exhausts destiny.
4) Inference: fine nasal intake to the lower “玄珠,” with spirit attending each breath, rebinds the pair.
5) Conclusion: immortality practice is fetal re-gestation of spirit upon yuan-qi, not external search.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Establish the lower abdominal “mysterious pearl” as the sole meeting point of attention and breath.
2) Ten to twenty gentle purifyings, then continuous fine breathing with spirit “seated” in the pearl.
3) For BaZi charts with broken 印 or exhausted 日主, train mothering qi before ambitious spirit work.
4) Cut external scheming during sessions; one thought = abortion of the embryo.
5) Use progressive time goals (100 days cohesion) rather than chasing visions.",
    "logic_compare": "Compared with 太无先生气经’s multi-technique curriculum, this text centers the single mother–child ontology. It is more neidan-proto than 中黄’s grain-expulsion narrative, and less liturgical than body-god Shangqing texts."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "唐玄宗御注道德真经",
    "logic_thesis": "Xuanzong’s commentary proves that the Dao is simultaneously a technique of self-rule and a constitution of the empire: the sage-king’s empty mind is the efficient cause of ordered society. By imperial gloss, Laozi is shown to authorize a political theology where non-coercive rule is the highest efficacy.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: the Daodejing speaks in double register—body and state, self and world.
2) Inference: imperial authority must be grounded in Dao, not only force or Confucian rite.
3) Inference: the ruler’s clarity, frugality, and non-contention model heaven’s way.
4) Inference: when the apex is quiet, the social body self-organizes.
5) Conclusion: correct reading of Laozi is a governing technology that unifies cultivation and polity.",
    "logic_practice": "1) In chart reading, treat the Day Master as “ruler of the state”; apply Xuanzong’s wuwei: do not force weak elements with violent remedies.
2) Prefer subtractive strategies (reduce desire, reduce over-control) when official stars are heavy.
3) Align personal schedule with seasonal economy—act less in dead seasons, store in living seasons.
4) Use leadership moments (官运) to practice empty authority: set conditions, avoid micromanagement.
5) Journal political–personal parallels: household chaos often mirrors internal contention.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike Song Huizong’s more mystical-ritual reading, Xuanzong’s note is classicist-political and stabilizing for Tang orthodoxy. It differs from purely eremitic neidan readings by insisting the Dao’s proof is public order as much as private longevity."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "道德真经传",
    "logic_thesis": "As a “transmission” commentary, it proves that the Daodejing is not a closed archaic poem but a living instructional chain: meaning is completed only when received, practiced, and re-spoken. The logic of 传 is that Dao authenticity is tested by continuity of understanding across persons, not by private cleverness.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: a classic without transmission decays into literary ornament.
2) Inference: each generation must re-articulate Laozi’s causal claims (return, softness, contentment) in usable form.
3) Inference: transmission selects what is effective for self-cultivation and order.
4) Inference: the text’s obscurities are pedagogical thresholds, not mere archaic style.
5) Conclusion: true “virtue” is proven when the teaching still produces quiet power in the receiver’s life.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Do not only read Laozi; keep a transmission notebook of what actually changed behavior.
2) Choose one chapter as a monthly operating rule (e.g., ch.16 for stillness in 印-weak charts).
3) Teach one insight to another person as a test of whether you truly received it.
4) In BaZi counseling, transmit one principle at a time; overload breaks 传.
5) Verify lineage of any method: who lived it, not only who marketed it.",
    "logic_compare": "It differs from imperial “御注/御解” by emphasizing pedagogical succession rather than sovereign monopoly of meaning. Compared with 道德真经论’s more discursive philosophizing, 传 stresses handed-down operability of the classic."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "宋徽宗御解道德真经",
    "logic_thesis": "Huizong’s explanation proves a more sacralized imperial Dao: the emperor-reader unites ritual aesthetics, inner subtlety, and cosmic sovereignty so that Laozi becomes a charter for theocratic culture. It argues that ultimate governance is resonance with the formless, expressed through refined forms of worship and art.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: the Dao is both formless source and source of all cultural forms.
2) Inference: the Song emperor’s role is to embody that source through ritual-civilizational refinement.
3) Inference: commentary therefore leans mystical, liturgical, and numinous rather than only administrative.
4) Inference: personal subtlety of the sovereign magnetizes the age’s qi.
5) Conclusion: reading Laozi is participation in a sacred cosmology where politics, art, and spirit cohere.",
    "logic_practice": "1) When a chart is rich in 食伤 and 财 (aesthetic production), use Huizong logic: refine form without losing emptiness.
2) Pair cultivation with one high-quality ritual or art act daily (incense, calligraphy, pure music).
3) Guard against the text’s historical warning: mystical sovereignty without earthy restraint risks excess—check 土 for grounding.
4) In peak 官印 luck, cultivate “resonance leadership” rather than coercion.
5) Balance beauty with simplicity; if form thickens, return to formless sitting.",
    "logic_compare": "Compared with Tang Xuanzong’s cooler statecraft reading, Huizong’s is warmer, more Daoist-churchly and aesthetic-theological. It differs from eremitic qi manuals by scaling cultivation to civilization itself, for better and worse."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "道德真经论",
    "logic_thesis": "As a treatise (论), it proves the Daodejing by argumentative reconstruction: Laozi’s paradoxes are resolved into a coherent theory of causation, value, and knowledge. It claims that the Dao can be discursively secured—softness over hardness, return over linear advance—without abandoning rational structure.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: apparent contradictions in Laozi invite systematic exposition.
2) Inference: key theses (non-contention, reversal, contented stop) are causal laws of success and failure.
3) Inference: discourse must show how these laws operate in self, society, and nature.
4) Inference: argument clears misreadings that turn Dao into either quietism or cunning strategy alone.
5) Conclusion: philosophical clarification is itself a cultivation of ming (clarity), preparing authentic practice.",
    "logic_practice": "1) For each life decision, write a one-page “论”: which Laozi law is at stake, and what evidence supports the softer path.
2) Use BaZi conflicts (官杀战, 财破印) as case studies for reversal strategies.
3) Train clarity before technique: understand why non-forcing works for your chart type.
4) Debate your own attachment positions weekly; let argument expose forced striving.
5) Convert conclusions into a single behavioral experiment for seven days.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike 传’s emphasis on lineage handoff and imperial notes’ political sacralization, 论 privileges reasoned system-building. It is closer to philosophical Daojia than to ritual Daojiao, preparing the mind before body methods of qi scriptures."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太上洞玄灵宝诸天内音自然玉字",
    "logic_thesis": "This Lingbao scripture proves that cosmos is a sonic-scriptural organism: each heaven’s “inner sound” and natural jade graphs are generative codes, not symbols added later. Salvation and cosmic repair occur when human voice re-enacts those primordial phonemes, re-synchronizing micro and macro order.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: heavens condensed from spontaneous jade characters and inner tones.
2) Inference: beings fall when they lose resonance with those tones.
3) Inference: correct chanting re-plugs the adept into the heaven that matches the sound.
4) Inference: multi-heaven liturgy therefore multiplies degrees of deliverance.
5) Conclusion: language at its root is ontology; liturgy is engineering of being.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Practice pure tone before semantic prayer; prioritize vibration quality and breath support.
2) Assign different heavenly sounds to different chart crises (fear, grief, anger) as tonal medicine.
3) Use regular recitation cycles (daily short, seasonal full) to build cumulative resonance.
4) In meditation, “hear” the body as a set of notes; correct the off-key organ through breath-sound.
5) For ancestral or death-related BaZi issues, use multi-heaven deliverance logic: sound reaches what argument cannot.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike Shangqing 三九素语 focused on body gates, this is a full heavenly polyphony of salvation. It differs from Beidou petition texts by asserting that graphs/sounds themselves are natural cosmic tissue, not only messages to officials."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太上洞玄灵宝三元品戒功德轻重经",
    "logic_thesis": "It proves that the moral universe is quantitative: the Three Origins’ graded precepts assign measurable weight to merit and demerit. Liberation is not vague sincerity but an accounting of actions under heavenly tribunals, making ethics a precise soteriological technology.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: heaven judges by Three Origin offices with graded rules.
2) Inference: deeds differ in gravity; not all faults or goods are equal.
3) Inference: knowing weights allows strategic repentance and cultivation of high-yield virtues.
4) Inference: ritual confession and precept-keeping alter the ledger that determines destiny.
5) Conclusion: spiritual progress is ethical bookkeeping under cosmic law, not only energetic technique.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Build a personal “merit ledger” aligned with Three Origins (heaven–earth–water / upper–middle–lower conduct).
2) Rank daily faults by weight; attack the heaviest first (harm to life, deceit, sexual chaos, etc.).
3) In BaZi years of 官杀 (judgment), intensify precept practice as legal defense.
4) Pair energetic work with concrete restitution actions—apology, return, service.
5) Review every new and full moon as mini Three-Origin audits.",
    "logic_compare": "Compared with pure qi or cunsi scriptures, this text relocates causality to moral weight. It differs from general “be good” preachments by insisting on graded severity and formal judgment structure characteristic of Lingbao communal religion."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太上洞玄灵宝灭度五炼生尸妙经",
    "logic_thesis": "It proves that death is a craftable transition: through five refinements, the corpse can be regenerated into a living spiritual body. Extinction (灭度) is not annihilation but a controlled metallurgical process of the person across the death boundary.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: ordinary death freezes unresolved qi into a corpse-state of bondage.
2) Inference: fivefold refining fires/processes reorganize the postmortem form.
3) Inference: liturgy supplies the missing cosmic agents the dead cannot summon alone.
4) Inference: successful refinement “生尸”—generates a living body from the corpse condition.
5) Conclusion: salvation includes funerary engineering; the Dao’s compassion operates at the limit of mortality.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Treat end-of-life and ancestral BaZi themes as refinement problems, not pure fate.
2) Practice “five refinements” in life as pre-death training: refine essence, breath, spirit, intent, and virtue.
3) For charts heavy with 七杀/死墓库, use periodic fasting, confession, and light rites as rehearsal of 灭度.
4) In family death work, prioritize orderly ritual over panic—structure is the five fires.
5) Meditate on bodily dissolution without terror, keeping a continuous point of awareness as the seed of the refined body.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike longevity manuals that try to avoid death, this scripture technologically redefines death. It differs from simple rebirth promises by specifying fivefold alchemical processing of the corpse within Lingbao deliverance liturgy."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太清中黄真经",
    "logic_thesis": "It proves that central yellow (spleen/earth/中黄) is the axis of transformation: by clearing grain toxins and feeding on pure qi, the middle palace becomes a fetal storehouse. True form is revealed only when turbid digestive residue ceases to mask spirit.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: ordinary diet leaves residual “grain essence” that binds organs and hosts the three worms.
2) Inference: progressive bigu and qi-feeding evacuate this residue.
3) Inference: the middle yellow center, once pure, can gestate embryonic breath and inner spirits.
4) Inference: abstinence from desire accelerates detoxification of both gut and mind.
5) Conclusion: immortality begins as gastroenteric-spiritual purification around the earth center.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Strengthen 土 in BaZi terms first if middle qi is weak; do not force fasting on collapsed earth.
2) Staged dietary simplification (not reckless starvation) while increasing breath nourishment.
3) Center practice on spleen–stomach calm: regular times, warm simplicity, less stimulation.
4) Watch for classic detox signs (turbidity leaving, fluctuating strength) without panic.
5) Combine with desire reduction; the text’s logic binds gut residue to craving residue.",
    "logic_compare": "Compared with 太无先生气经, it is more toxin-and-bigu centered and poetic-esoteric. Compared with 五厨经, it is more physiological-elimination than mind-kitchen metaphysics, though both redirect nourishment from food to qi."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "太上老君说五厨经",
    "logic_thesis": "Laozi’s Five Kitchens prove that true alimentation is directional qi feeding the five viscera: when mind is one and qi is harmonized to the five directions, hunger and depletion lose their ordinary grip. The kitchen is internal cosmology; thinking and qi distribution cook immortality.",
    "logic_chain": "1) Premise: the five organs are five cosmic kitchens requiring proper “dishes” of qi.
2) Inference: mental agitation burns the provisions; unity of mind conserves them.
3) Inference: verses/methods of the five directions supply organ-specific nourishment without grain.
4) Inference: balanced five-kitchen feeding yields lightness, clarity, and extended life.
5) Conclusion: nutrition is a spiritual distribution problem solved by one-pointed harmony with the five qi.",
    "logic_practice": "1) Map five organs to BaZi elements; feed the deficient organ with matching directional breath and calm.
2) Before meals or instead of stress-eating, recite/hold the corresponding kitchen intent for 9 breaths.
3) Use emotional diagnostics: anger burns liver kitchen; worry collapses spleen kitchen—repair with the matching method.
4) Practice one-meal or reduced-meal days only after five-qi balance is felt.
5) Keep mind unified during intake of air or food; distracted eating is a broken kitchen.",
    "logic_compare": "Unlike 中黄真经’s emphasis on expelling grain residue, 五厨经 emphasizes positive cosmic refeeding via fivefold mind-qi. It is shorter, more mental-cosmic, and less stepwise technical than 太无气经, while sharing the anti-ordinary-food soteriology."
  },
  {
    "name_han": "皇极经世",
    "logic_thesis": "Shao Yong proves that history and cosmos are one calculable organism: yuan–hui–yun–shi cycles make time a hierarchical number system isomorphic with hexagram order. By “observing things as things,” the sage reads rise and fall without selfish distortion, turning chronology into moral-cosmic science.",

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that Quanzhen orthodoxy is historically verifiable rather than merely mythic: legitimacy is generated by synchronized, datable lives of Wang Chongyang and the Seven Perfected. By collapsing eight biographies into one chronological frame, it argues that collective time-discipline—not isolated miracle—constitutes the real transmission of the Dao.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: a living lineage must be reconstructed as continuous, dated events, not floating hagiography.
2) Inference: Wang Chongyang’s conversion of seven disciples is the causal hinge of later Quanzhen expansion.
3) Inference: each Perfected’s subsequent itinerary, hardship, and teaching is evidence of the same method under different temperaments.
4) Inference: chronological alignment converts personal cultivation stories into public institutional history.
5) Conclusion: Quanzhen authority rests on demonstrable succession in historical time, which is itself a spiritual proof of “completing the true.”
entries.logic_practice:
1) When reading a BaZi chart, treat the natal pattern as a “谱” (register): map decade luck as sequential stages of a life-lineage, not random fortune.
2) Extract one core discipline from each Seven Perfected style (clear mind, endurance, stillness, social service) and match it to the chart’s weak element.
3) Use historical dates as models for timing renunciation or career pivots in the current luck cycle.
4) Practice “collective verification”: check cultivation progress against measurable life events, as the nianpu does against chronology.
5) Treat teacher–disciple transfer as a timed transmission event; note stem-branch years of initiation for lineage work.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure miracle hagiographies, this work subordinates marvel to calendar. It differs from 金莲正宗记 by prioritizing year-by-year sequence over narrative glory, and differs from purely doctrinal Quanzhen texts by proving the path through temporal evidence rather than abstract xingming theory.

entries.logic_thesis: The text argues that place is a causal agent of sanctity: Zhongnan Mountain’s ancestral court concentrates earlier Daoist virtue so later Quanzhen can inherit it as spatial transmission. Inner biography of “仙真” proves that orthodoxy is not invented at one founder but accumulated in a sacred geography that selects and ripens adepts.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: authentic Dao must have a stable “祖庭” (ancestral court) where true persons gather across generations.
2) Inference: earlier immortals of Zhongnan form a pre-Quanzhen spiritual deposit.
3) Inference: Wang Chongyang and his heirs re-activate that deposit rather than create a vacuum religion.
4) Inference: biography of place-bound immortals legitimates institutional claim to the mountain.
5) Conclusion: geographic continuity equals doctrinal continuity; the mountain “remembers” the Dao.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In BaZi, treat strong mountain/earth structures (辰戌丑未, 艮坤) as “祖庭” nodes—places where ancestral qi can be cultivated.
2) When luck shifts to earth or mountain-related branches, prioritize retreat, temple practice, or root-clearing over travel.
3) Map personal “sacred sites” (birthplace, teacher’s mountain, burial of parents) as transmission fields.
4) Use inner biography method: write your own cultivation chronology tied to places, not only moods.
5) For lineage work, verify whether a method has a stable “court” (school form) or is free-floating charisma.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 七真年谱, this text proves by sacred space rather than calendar alone. Unlike pure Shangqing mountain-revelation scriptures, it is Quanzhen-historiographical: it harnesses older Zhongnan lore to authorize a new school’s claim to the ancestral seat.

entries.name_han: 太微帝君二十四神回元经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the body is already a full pantheon: twenty-four gods of the three regions are not external deities but structural officers of jing, qi, and spirit. “Returning to origin” is accomplished by naming, visualizing, and reinstalling these officers so that scattered vitality re-coheres into the Taiwei order.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: human form is generated by mixed qi and therefore contains named inner deities as functional centers.
2) Inference: disease, leakage, and death are failures of those officers to stay at their posts.
3) Inference: cunsi (visualization) of names and colors reassigns each god to its region.
4) Inference: prolonged reinstallation opens the “return to yuan,” dissolving fetal knots and stagnation.
5) Conclusion: immortality technique is administrative restoration of the body-state under Taiwei Emperor’s hierarchical order.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Divide practice into three octaves (upper/middle/lower eight gods) aligned with three dantian and three BaZi “talents” (spirit, officer, wealth).
2) On the birth day or monthly jing day, recite the 24 names while scanning the corresponding body zones.
3) When a chart shows scattered 印/食伤 (leaking resources), treat it as gods off-post; use stillness to “call them back.”
4) Pair each god with a color–direction correspondence for microcosmic orientation.
5) Measure progress by cohesion of attention and reduced leakage (senses, speech, desire), not visionary fireworks.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Beidou liturgical texts that petition external star-lords, this scripture interiorizes the hierarchy into body-gods. It differs from later neidan’s abstract three treasures by retaining early Shangqing polytheistic administration as the logic of unity.

entries.name_han: 太上紫微中天七元真经
entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that destiny is editable at the register level: the Seven Yuan of the Northern Dipper hold the ledger of life, so ritual sound, light, and talisman can rewrite entries of disaster and lifespan. Cosmic government at Purple Tenuity is not fatalism; it is a bureaucracy open to lawful petition.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: human lifespan and calamity are recorded under the Seven Dipper lords.
2) Inference: each lord governs a distinct mode of protection (birth, obstacle-removal, illness, etc.).
3) Inference: recitation, lamp-offering, and visualization create a legal channel to those registers.
4) Inference: when the name is “noted above,” form and hun-po are guarded.
5) Conclusion: salvation is ledger correction under Zhongtian Zǐwēi, not mere psychological comfort.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Map the seven Dipper stars to the seven day-masters’ typical crisis modes; choose the matching mantra for the active luck crisis.
2) On the monthly Dipper days or birth hour, perform lamp-and-incense petition focused on one lord, not all at once.
3) In BaZi terms, treat severe 七杀/羊刃 years as “register pressure”; use 七元 work as official appeal, not denial of pattern.
4) Combine oral spell with steady breath so “sound” actually enters the body register.
5) Keep a simple response log (sleep, omens, event shifts) to verify ledger change without superstition.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 太微二十四神回元经’s inward body bureaucracy, this text works an outer stellar bureaucracy. It is leaner and more liturgical than the longer Beidou benming scriptures, focusing on seven modular spells rather than full narrative theology.

entries.name_han: 洞真太上三九素语玉精真诀
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that pure speech is an ontological key: “three-nine plain words” are not poetry but engineered phonemes that open the nine orifices and three palaces. Jade-essence truth is recovered when correct sound unlocks closed spirit-gates, making longevity a function of linguistic precision rather than brute force effort.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the body has sealed spirit-gates (ling guan) that ordinary thought cannot open.
2) Inference: primordial emperors condensed “素语” as keys to those gates.
3) Inference: timed silent/voiced recitation on benming days reorders qi in nine holes and three palaces.
4) Inference: when gates open, organs freshen, complexion becomes jade-like, and true beings respond.
5) Conclusion: verbal formula is a technical instrument of physiological and celestial access.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Practice short, exact recitation rather than long discursive prayer; precision beats volume.
2) Schedule work on the natal day (本命日) when the chart’s “door” is naturally more permeable.
3) Coordinate three palaces (head–chest–abdomen) with nine breaths as a 3×9 structure.
4) If BaZi shows sealed 印星 or blocked 食伤 (expression blocked), use plain-word practice to open the speech–spirit circuit.
5) Keep secrecy and vow discipline: the text’s logic treats leakage of formula as loss of charge.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Lingbao “inner sounds of the heavens,” this is Shangqing body-gate technology rather than multi-heaven salvation liturgy. It differs from later mantric popularism by insisting on elite transmission, timed use, and physiological gate theory.

entries.name_han: 上清外国放品青童内文
entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that true power is topographic knowledge of non-ordinary realms: foreign countries, hidden lands, and thirty-six heavens are structured domains whose secret names grant mobility, exorcism, and immunity. Salvation is cartographic—knowing the right graph and sound lets the adept cross boundaries that trap the uninitiated.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the cosmos contains graded “foreign products/realms” beyond ordinary geography.
2) Inference: each realm has inner names, graphs, and sounds that function as passports.
3) Inference: wearing, reciting, or visualizing these texts enrolls the adept in those jurisdictions.
4) Inference: enrollment subdues demons, opens mountains, and enables spirit travel.
5) Conclusion: liberation is mastery of sacred topology via the Azure Lad’s transmitted inner writing.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Treat BaZi’s four pillars as a personal “map of realms”; identify blocked directions as locked countries.
2) When luck moves into travel or 驿马 years, pair ordinary movement with name-recitation for protection.
3) Use directional talismanic focus (east text for east crises, etc.) instead of generic prayer.
4) In meditation, practice “border crossing”: leave sensory realm, enter named heaven, return with stable identity.
5) Apply exorcistic logic ethically: name what binds you (habit, ghostly fear, social hex) and revoke its jurisdiction.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike body-god cunsi texts that stay inside the flesh, this scripture expands outward into cosmic ethnography. It differs from Lingbao universal heavens by retaining Shangqing elite secrecy and “foreign country” adventure structure under the Azure Lad transmission.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves a strict causal law of embodiment: form depends on qi; qi depends on form; therefore longevity is engineered by staged internal breathing, not by swallowing external cosmic winds. True method is progressive interiorization from coarse regulation to fetal breath, grounded in “my destiny is in me.”
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: form and qi are mutually constitutive; lose one and the other dies.
2) Inference: external qi methods are crude and can harm if interior is not ready.
3) Inference: genuine work uses the body’s own internal qi through graded arts (调、咽、行、炼、闭, etc.).
4) Inference: constancy plus emptiness of desire allows true qi to descend and stabilize.
5) Conclusion: destiny is reclaimed by disciplined neigì sequence, not fatalist heaven or random gulping of air.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Begin with environment and schedule (dry quiet room, post-midnight or empty stomach) before advanced retention.
2) Sequence practice: expel turbid → regulate → swallow saliva-qi → move → refine → entrust → close.
3) In BaZi weak-qi charts (feeble 日主, damaged 印), prioritize gentle neigì over aggressive fasting.
4) Use grip-seal (握固) only after circulation is open, matching the text’s staged caution.
5) Track sweat, warmth, calm hunger, and sleep as objective markers of qi sufficiency.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Shangqing visionary pantheons, this is technical respiratory engineering. Compared with 中黄真经, it is more stepwise pedagogical and less focused on grain-toxin theory; compared with 五厨经, it is more somatic technique than mind-nourishment philosophy.

entries.logic_thesis: The text argues that the highest method must be portable and immediately usable—“behind the elbow,” always at hand. Jade-scripture formulas compress esoteric efficacy into compact prescriptions, proving that Daoist truth is not only grand cosmology but emergency-ready operational knowledge.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: adepts face sudden crises that lengthy ritual cannot address in time.
2) Inference: authentic transmission therefore includes condensed “elbow-side” formulas.
3) Inference: compact jade methods retain full structural logic of larger systems in miniature.
4) Inference: diligent private application produces spiritual effect without institutional theater.
5) Conclusion: true mastery is the ability to deploy the Dao as a pocketed, exact remedy.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Distill your BaZi remedy into 1–3 “elbow formulas” (one breath pattern, one behavioral vow, one timing rule).
2) Keep a daily micro-protocol that can be done in under ten minutes under stress.
3) Prefer small consistent doses of practice over rare grand retreats.
4) When luck is chaotic, use the portable method first; expand only after stability returns.
5) Record which compact formula works for which pillar stress (wealth month vs officer year).
entries.logic_compare: It differs from encyclopedic qi scriptures by valuing brevity and readiness. Unlike imperial Daodejing commentaries that scale Dao to statecraft, this is field medicine for the solitary body—operational Dao rather than metaphysical exposition.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that longevity is the correct mother–child relation of qi and spirit: qi is mother, spirit is child; the child must ride the mother’s breath without losing the embryonic pearl. Long life is not accumulation of years but continuous re-enactment of the original generative bond inside the lower yuan.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: what generates life (胎元) can also regenerate life if repaired.
2) Inference: form arises from subtle qi; spirit arises after form-qi are established.
3) Inference: disordered thought breaks the mother–child link and exhausts destiny.
4) Inference: fine nasal intake to the lower “玄珠,” with spirit attending each breath, rebinds the pair.
5) Conclusion: immortality practice is fetal re-gestation of spirit upon yuan-qi, not external search.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Establish the lower abdominal “mysterious pearl” as the sole meeting point of attention and breath.
2) Ten to twenty gentle purifyings, then continuous fine breathing with spirit “seated” in the pearl.
3) For BaZi charts with broken 印 or exhausted 日主, train mothering qi before ambitious spirit work.
4) Cut external scheming during sessions; one thought = abortion of the embryo.
5) Use progressive time goals (100 days cohesion) rather than chasing visions.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 太无先生气经’s multi-technique curriculum, this text centers the single mother–child ontology. It is more neidan-proto than 中黄’s grain-expulsion narrative, and less liturgical than body-god Shangqing texts.

entries.logic_thesis: Xuanzong’s commentary proves that the Dao is simultaneously a technique of self-rule and a constitution of the empire: the sage-king’s empty mind is the efficient cause of ordered society. By imperial gloss, Laozi is shown to authorize a political theology where non-coercive rule is the highest efficacy.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the Daodejing speaks in double register—body and state, self and world.
2) Inference: imperial authority must be grounded in Dao, not only force or Confucian rite.
3) Inference: the ruler’s clarity, frugality, and non-contention model heaven’s way.
4) Inference: when the apex is quiet, the social body self-organizes.
5) Conclusion: correct reading of Laozi is a governing technology that unifies cultivation and polity.
entries.logic_practice:
1) In chart reading, treat the Day Master as “ruler of the state”; apply Xuanzong’s wuwei: do not force weak elements with violent remedies.
2) Prefer subtractive strategies (reduce desire, reduce over-control) when official stars are heavy.
3) Align personal schedule with seasonal economy—act less in dead seasons, store in living seasons.
4) Use leadership moments (官运) to practice empty authority: set conditions, avoid micromanagement.
5) Journal political–personal parallels: household chaos often mirrors internal contention.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Song Huizong’s more mystical-ritual reading, Xuanzong’s note is classicist-political and stabilizing for Tang orthodoxy. It differs from purely eremitic neidan readings by insisting the Dao’s proof is public order as much as private longevity.

entries.logic_thesis: As a “transmission” commentary, it proves that the Daodejing is not a closed archaic poem but a living instructional chain: meaning is completed only when received, practiced, and re-spoken. The logic of 传 is that Dao authenticity is tested by continuity of understanding across persons, not by private cleverness.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: a classic without transmission decays into literary ornament.
2) Inference: each generation must re-articulate Laozi’s causal claims (return, softness, contentment) in usable form.
3) Inference: transmission selects what is effective for self-cultivation and order.
4) Inference: the text’s obscurities are pedagogical thresholds, not mere archaic style.
5) Conclusion: true “virtue” is proven when the teaching still produces quiet power in the receiver’s life.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Do not only read Laozi; keep a transmission notebook of what actually changed behavior.
2) Choose one chapter as a monthly operating rule (e.g., ch.16 for stillness in 印-weak charts).
3) Teach one insight to another person as a test of whether you truly received it.
4) In BaZi counseling, transmit one principle at a time; overload breaks 传.
5) Verify lineage of any method: who lived it, not only who marketed it.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from imperial “御注/御解” by emphasizing pedagogical succession rather than sovereign monopoly of meaning. Compared with 道德真经论’s more discursive philosophizing, 传 stresses handed-down operability of the classic.

entries.logic_thesis: Huizong’s explanation proves a more sacralized imperial Dao: the emperor-reader unites ritual aesthetics, inner subtlety, and cosmic sovereignty so that Laozi becomes a charter for theocratic culture. It argues that ultimate governance is resonance with the formless, expressed through refined forms of worship and art.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the Dao is both formless source and source of all cultural forms.
2) Inference: the Song emperor’s role is to embody that source through ritual-civilizational refinement.
3) Inference: commentary therefore leans mystical, liturgical, and numinous rather than only administrative.
4) Inference: personal subtlety of the sovereign magnetizes the age’s qi.
5) Conclusion: reading Laozi is participation in a sacred cosmology where politics, art, and spirit cohere.
entries.logic_practice:
1) When a chart is rich in 食伤 and 财 (aesthetic production), use Huizong logic: refine form without losing emptiness.
2) Pair cultivation with one high-quality ritual or art act daily (incense, calligraphy, pure music).
3) Guard against the text’s historical warning: mystical sovereignty without earthy restraint risks excess—check 土 for grounding.
4) In peak 官印 luck, cultivate “resonance leadership” rather than coercion.
5) Balance beauty with simplicity; if form thickens, return to formless sitting.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Tang Xuanzong’s cooler statecraft reading, Huizong’s is warmer, more Daoist-churchly and aesthetic-theological. It differs from eremitic qi manuals by scaling cultivation to civilization itself, for better and worse.

entries.logic_thesis: As a treatise (论), it proves the Daodejing by argumentative reconstruction: Laozi’s paradoxes are resolved into a coherent theory of causation, value, and knowledge. It claims that the Dao can be discursively secured—softness over hardness, return over linear advance—without abandoning rational structure.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: apparent contradictions in Laozi invite systematic exposition.
2) Inference: key theses (non-contention, reversal, contented stop) are causal laws of success and failure.
3) Inference: discourse must show how these laws operate in self, society, and nature.
4) Inference: argument clears misreadings that turn Dao into either quietism or cunning strategy alone.
5) Conclusion: philosophical clarification is itself a cultivation of ming (clarity), preparing authentic practice.
entries.logic_practice:
1) For each life decision, write a one-page “论”: which Laozi law is at stake, and what evidence supports the softer path.
2) Use BaZi conflicts (官杀战, 财破印) as case studies for reversal strategies.
3) Train clarity before technique: understand why non-forcing works for your chart type.
4) Debate your own attachment positions weekly; let argument expose forced striving.
5) Convert conclusions into a single behavioral experiment for seven days.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 传’s emphasis on lineage handoff and imperial notes’ political sacralization, 论 privileges reasoned system-building. It is closer to philosophical Daojia than to ritual Daojiao, preparing the mind before body methods of qi scriptures.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄灵宝诸天内音自然玉字
entries.logic_thesis: This Lingbao scripture proves that cosmos is a sonic-scriptural organism: each heaven’s “inner sound” and natural jade graphs are generative codes, not symbols added later. Salvation and cosmic repair occur when human voice re-enacts those primordial phonemes, re-synchronizing micro and macro order.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: heavens condensed from spontaneous jade characters and inner tones.
2) Inference: beings fall when they lose resonance with those tones.
3) Inference: correct chanting re-plugs the adept into the heaven that matches the sound.
4) Inference: multi-heaven liturgy therefore multiplies degrees of deliverance.
5) Conclusion: language at its root is ontology; liturgy is engineering of being.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Practice pure tone before semantic prayer; prioritize vibration quality and breath support.
2) Assign different heavenly sounds to different chart crises (fear, grief, anger) as tonal medicine.
3) Use regular recitation cycles (daily short, seasonal full) to build cumulative resonance.
4) In meditation, “hear” the body as a set of notes; correct the off-key organ through breath-sound.
5) For ancestral or death-related BaZi issues, use multi-heaven deliverance logic: sound reaches what argument cannot.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Shangqing 三九素语 focused on body gates, this is a full heavenly polyphony of salvation. It differs from Beidou petition texts by asserting that graphs/sounds themselves are natural cosmic tissue, not only messages to officials.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄灵宝三元品戒功德轻重经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the moral universe is quantitative: the Three Origins’ graded precepts assign measurable weight to merit and demerit. Liberation is not vague sincerity but an accounting of actions under heavenly tribunals, making ethics a precise soteriological technology.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: heaven judges by Three Origin offices with graded rules.
2) Inference: deeds differ in gravity; not all faults or goods are equal.
3) Inference: knowing weights allows strategic repentance and cultivation of high-yield virtues.
4) Inference: ritual confession and precept-keeping alter the ledger that determines destiny.
5) Conclusion: spiritual progress is ethical bookkeeping under cosmic law, not only energetic technique.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Build a personal “merit ledger” aligned with Three Origins (heaven–earth–water / upper–middle–lower conduct).
2) Rank daily faults by weight; attack the heaviest first (harm to life, deceit, sexual chaos, etc.).
3) In BaZi years of 官杀 (judgment), intensify precept practice as legal defense.
4) Pair energetic work with concrete restitution actions—apology, return, service.
5) Review every new and full moon as mini Three-Origin audits.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with pure qi or cunsi scriptures, this text relocates causality to moral weight. It differs from general “be good” preachments by insisting on graded severity and formal judgment structure characteristic of Lingbao communal religion.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄灵宝灭度五炼生尸妙经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that death is a craftable transition: through five refinements, the corpse can be regenerated into a living spiritual body. Extinction (灭度) is not annihilation but a controlled metallurgical process of the person across the death boundary.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: ordinary death freezes unresolved qi into a corpse-state of bondage.
2) Inference: fivefold refining fires/processes reorganize the postmortem form.
3) Inference: liturgy supplies the missing cosmic agents the dead cannot summon alone.
4) Inference: successful refinement “生尸”—generates a living body from the corpse condition.
5) Conclusion: salvation includes funerary engineering; the Dao’s compassion operates at the limit of mortality.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Treat end-of-life and ancestral BaZi themes as refinement problems, not pure fate.
2) Practice “five refinements” in life as pre-death training: refine essence, breath, spirit, intent, and virtue.
3) For charts heavy with 七杀/死墓库, use periodic fasting, confession, and light rites as rehearsal of 灭度.
4) In family death work, prioritize orderly ritual over panic—structure is the five fires.
5) Meditate on bodily dissolution without terror, keeping a continuous point of awareness as the seed of the refined body.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike longevity manuals that try to avoid death, this scripture technologically redefines death. It differs from simple rebirth promises by specifying fivefold alchemical processing of the corpse within Lingbao deliverance liturgy.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that central yellow (spleen/earth/中黄) is the axis of transformation: by clearing grain toxins and feeding on pure qi, the middle palace becomes a fetal storehouse. True form is revealed only when turbid digestive residue ceases to mask spirit.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: ordinary diet leaves residual “grain essence” that binds organs and hosts the three worms.
2) Inference: progressive bigu and qi-feeding evacuate this residue.
3) Inference: the middle yellow center, once pure, can gestate embryonic breath and inner spirits.
4) Inference: abstinence from desire accelerates detoxification of both gut and mind.
5) Conclusion: immortality begins as gastroenteric-spiritual purification around the earth center.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Strengthen 土 in BaZi terms first if middle qi is weak; do not force fasting on collapsed earth.
2) Staged dietary simplification (not reckless starvation) while increasing breath nourishment.
3) Center practice on spleen–stomach calm: regular times, warm simplicity, less stimulation.
4) Watch for classic detox signs (turbidity leaving, fluctuating strength) without panic.
5) Combine with desire reduction; the text’s logic binds gut residue to craving residue.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 太无先生气经, it is more toxin-and-bigu centered and poetic-esoteric. Compared with 五厨经, it is more physiological-elimination than mind-kitchen metaphysics, though both redirect nourishment from food to qi.

entries.logic_thesis: Laozi’s Five Kitchens prove that true alimentation is directional qi feeding the five viscera: when mind is one and qi is harmonized to the five directions, hunger and depletion lose their ordinary grip. The kitchen is internal cosmology; thinking and qi distribution cook immortality.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: the five organs are five cosmic kitchens requiring proper “dishes” of qi.
2) Inference: mental agitation burns the provisions; unity of mind conserves them.
3) Inference: verses/methods of the five directions supply organ-specific nourishment without grain.
4) Inference: balanced five-kitchen feeding yields lightness, clarity, and extended life.
5) Conclusion: nutrition is a spiritual distribution problem solved by one-pointed harmony with the five qi.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Map five organs to BaZi elements; feed the deficient organ with matching directional breath and calm.
2) Before meals or instead of stress-eating, recite/hold the corresponding kitchen intent for 9 breaths.
3) Use emotional diagnostics: anger burns liver kitchen; worry collapses spleen kitchen—repair with the matching method.
4) Practice one-meal or reduced-meal days only after five-qi balance is felt.
5) Keep mind unified during intake of air or food; distracted eating is a broken kitchen.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 中黄真经’s emphasis on expelling grain residue, 五厨经 emphasizes positive cosmic refeeding via fivefold mind-qi. It is shorter, more mental-cosmic, and less stepwise technical than 太无气经, while sharing the anti-ordinary-food soteriology.

entries.logic_thesis: Shao Yong proves that history and cosmos are one calculable organism: yuan–hui–yun–shi cycles make time a hierarchical number system isomorphic with hexagram order. By “observing things as things,” the sage reads rise and fall without selfish distortion, turning chronology into moral-cosmic science.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: heaven’s time is structured like nested calendrical multiples (12/30 symmetries).
2) Inference: one yuan of 129,600 years frames all lesser ages of politics and nature.
3) Inference: events can be ordered under hexagrams and numerical seasons of destiny.
4) Inference: correct knowing requires 以物观物—disinterested, object-true observation.
5) Conclusion: prophecy and philosophy meet: the pattern of the world is intelligible, cyclic, and ethically legible.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Nest personal BaZi inside larger cycles: year luck < decade < historical generation < yuan-scale climate of the age.
2) Practice disinterested observation for seven days: describe events without “I like/I fear” to train 观物.
3) When judging a luck shift, ask which scale is moving (month noise vs decade structure).
4) Use Shao’s hierarchy to avoid over-reading small omens as civilizational fate—and vice versa.
5) Build a life timeline in 30-year “世” blocks to see recurring moral causes of rise/fall.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Daoist liturgical heavens or Quanzhen hagiography, this is Confucian-Daoist numerical cosmology of history. It differs from ordinary BaZi by scaling from individual charts to civilizational time, providing the macro-clock within which natal charts tick.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves Quanzhen identity as a “golden lotus” orthodox chain: legitimacy is narrative purity of patriarchs and Seven Perfected, arranged to show one flowering school. By selective sacred history, it argues that correct practice is inseparable from correct lineage story.
entries.logic_chain:
1) Premise: a school under pressure needs an authoritative origin myth-history.
2) Inference: the golden lotus image unifies multiple saints into one plant of orthodoxy.
3) Inference: biographies of founders and Seven Perfected model the virtues that define the school.
4) Inference: readers inherit identity by recognizing themselves inside that story.
5) Conclusion: narrative canonization is a spiritual technology of institutional and personal alignment.
entries.logic_practice:
1) Write your cultivation as a “lotus register”: teachers, vows, crises, recoveries—one stem.
2) Extract Seven Perfected virtues and assign them to the seven days of a practice week.
3) When BaZi shows identity confusion (strong 比劫 battle), stabilize by choosing one orthodox method-story and stopping mixing.
4) Use hagiography as mirror, not cosplay: emulate structure of renunciation and service, not costume.
5) In community, transmit stories that encode discipline, not celebrity miracles alone.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 七真年谱’s chronological austerity, 金莲正宗记 is more literary-orthodox and identity-forming. Unlike Zhongnan 内传’s place-based legitimation, it centers a symbol (golden lotus) and a portable pan-lineage narrative for Quanzhen self-understanding.
